bible.tagline: Note 0 is bottom-left. Channel is track. Centre is everything.

decks.name: The Grid
decks.world: The 5x8 pad grid drawn on a matte black chassis: note 0 bottom-left, rows of eight, five rows for five layers, the 128-entry RGB velocity palette, the two LED families every pack here speaks (green 21/22, amber 9/10), the Scene Launch column, and the SysEx that puts the controller into Mode 1 - a show requirement, because a power cycle forgets it.

palette.why: Silkscreen white, protocol values in Consolas.
MIDI red, only on the wire.

moments: Note zero: Scene Launch 1 and press the real bottom-left pad; the picture is the pad.
Palette: column 4, tap the row-3 FIGURE pad on the beat so index 9 blinks amber over the 128-cell table.
Mode 1: UP to column 8 and let the SysEx bytes ride the mids; this is the message to send after every power-up.

decks.name: The Strips
decks.world: Eight track strips, each a copy of the last: the per-track buttons keep one note and change only the MIDI channel. Clip Stop 52 ejects, Select 51 selects, Activator 50 is on-air, Solo 49, Record Arm 48 and Crossfade A/B 66 are the first two effect banks in every pack here. Below them the eight faders on CC7, the master on CC14 and the crossfader on CC15 whose centre is everything.
moments: Channel = track: Scene Launch 1, then press Clip Stop on strip 3 - the one lit button (layer 3) vanishes, because note 52 on channel 3 ejects layer 3; Scene Launch 1 brings it back.
Rec Arm: column 5, tap the real Record Arm buttons - they are FX bank 1, and the amber row is them.
Crossfader: column 8, sweep the real crossfader; the scene's layers split A from B (the green cap sits on FIGURE, side B, and goes dark at hard A). The cap's own travel is the lows, not CC15.

decks.name: Knobs + Transport
decks.world: The right-hand block and the top row: eight Device knobs with LED rings on CC16-23 (the dashboard links), eight Track knobs on CC48-55 (the live FFT), Cue Level on CC47 (the effects master sweep), the relative Tempo encoder on CC13, PLAY STOP RECORD on notes 91-93, Tap and Nudge, and the footswitch on CC64 that is a momentary blackout in every pack here.

palette.why: Red for relative ticks and the footswitch.

moments: Rings: column 2, turn Device knob 1 slowly; the amber ring on screen is the ring under your hand.
Cue level: column 4, sweep CUE LEVEL anticlockwise to CLEAN and back; the amber line is the four bank links moving together.
Footswitch: column 8, stamp the pedal on the one; the red bar is CC64 going 0x7F.

decks.name: The Wire
decks.world: MIDI itself, from the 1983 spec to tonight's preset: the DIN-5 with its 5 mA current loop, 31,250 baud and ten bits a byte, the status byte with its high bit set, note on and note off (Piano listens for the off), control change with 128 steps, the class-compliant USB that powers the whole surface, and the 2^56 (note) and 2^57 (CC) markers Resolume files a raw message under. Red is the wire; green is a message arriving.
moments: Baud: Scene Launch 2 and the bit stream rides the mids; on the five-pin wire every byte is ten bits (the APC rides USB, which packs them four bytes at a time).
Note on/off: column 4, hold a pad - the green pad lives while you hold it, the flash is the note off.
Monitor: column 8 with Preferences > MIDI open on the second screen; the scrolling line is what the monitor shows.

decks.name: SE-500 Mixer
decks.world: A four-input analog SD video mixer drawn in the same chassis grammar: BNC composite and S-Video inputs with illuminated select buttons, a main and a sub source bus, the T-bar you pull at your own speed, wipes, picture-in-picture, split screen, colour processing, and - the reason it belongs in this pack - RS-232 on a 9-pin D-sub and MIDI control on a five-pin DIN: the APC40's language on the older wire (the APC itself is USB-only).

palette.why: The pack's lit green (the SE-500's own on-air colour is red).

moments: T-bar: Scene Launch 3 and ride the real crossfader slowly end to end; the amber T-bar is your hand.
Wipe to PIP: UP from Wipe to PIP on a downbeat with Device knob 3 (SPACE) at a quarter and MIRROR QUAD lit so the window tiles.
The older wire: column 8, tap any APC button on the beat; the red pins flash - the same note-on, on five pins instead of USB.

effect_wishlist.role: Bank A: LED bleed through the rubber.
Bank A: the T-bar's travel and the bit stream.
Bank D: the PIP window tiles.
Bank C: the mixer's program monitor.
Bank D: the pad grid of grids.

bible.fft_philosophy: The controller is the subject and the music is what it controls, so the reactivity stays mechanical: lows swell pads and widen fader caps, mids turn knob gaps and move playheads and T-bars, highs only jitter the serial bits and the DIN pins. Colour never reacts: green is a lit pad or a message arriving, amber is the second LED family and the T-bar, red is the wire and nothing else. Text never moves. Every note, CC and byte on screen is the real one.
bible.wildcard_rationale: Four decks are the APC40 mkII and its wire: the grid, the strips, the knobs and transport, and MIDI itself. The fifth is a video mixer of the same era of hands-on control, the Datavideo SE-500, chosen because it speaks the APC's MIDI over the older five-pin wire and because its T-bar is the crossfader's older sibling.
